title: When the Language Burns
premise: Ivo Whitlock, a piano tuner who reads a building's past in its pipes and radiators, has spent eleven years as a caretaker-tenant in the house where his late sister Lena once lived and wrote songs she never recorded. When he hears one of those songs on the radio — credited to another man — Ivo is forced to confront the theft of her work and his own silence at the time of her death. His search for justice takes him outside the courts, into the memory of the old neighborhood slated for demolition and rerouting. The novel ends with Ivo performing Lena's song aloud on the last bus before its route disappears, saying goodbye properly at last, and choosing to buy the house rather than merely inhabit it.
about_author: Mirabel Ishikawa is the pen name of a former piano restorer who spent a decade tuning instruments in condemned buildings across the industrial North. She writes about sound, inheritance, and the small justices people make when institutions fail them.

chapters.title: The Radiator Speaks First
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He tunes a piano in a dying house, narrating the building's history through its heating pipes, and establishes his tenant's detachment from his own life. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Someone Else's Lease
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashbacks braid with present-day routine; we learn he inherited the tenancy after his sister Lena's death and never signed anything permanent. Beat: grief kept functional by avoidance.

chapters.title: A Song He Knows by Its Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Driving home, the radio plays an unfamiliar melody that is unmistakably Lena's unfinished song, credited to producer Dale Merrick. Ivo pulls over, shaking. Beat: the buried past detonating in ordinary time.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He searches the house for Lena's notebooks, listening to radiators like archives, and finds a page of lyrics hidden behind a radiator panel. Beat: hope rekindled, guilt sharpened.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns Her Voice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ivo researches Dale Merrick, now celebrated; brief Merrick POV shows a man who believes possession is authorship. Beat: injustice given a face and a plausible self-justification.

chapters.title: Neighbors of the Vanished Street
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He visits the old neighborhood, half-demolished, and meets Odile, Lena's former bandmate, who confirms the song's origin but warns him the law won't help. Beat: belonging rediscovered among the displaced.

chapters.title: Papers Don't Hum
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She recounts the night Lena played the song for Merrick, and why no recording exists — Lena refused studios. Beat: the theme of justice outside the law crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Tenant Who Never Unpacked
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A landlord's notice arrives: the house will be sold. Ivo realizes he has protected nothing — not the house, not the songs, not himself. Beat: stakes made personal and material.

chapters.title: Letters to a Dead Address
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He drafts a letter to Merrick and burns it; instead he begins cataloguing every song Lena left in pipes, floorboards, and notebooks. Beat: turning from accusation to testimony.

chapters.title: Merrick's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Merrick's POV. Confronted indirectly through his label, he deflects with lawyers and charm; Ivo learns the statute of limitations has passed. Beat: despair — the legal door closes.

chapters.title: The Last Bus Timetable
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The city announces the old route will be permanently rerouted in three weeks. Ivo fixates on the deadline as if the bus itself were a witness. Beat: urgency enters the story's bloodstream.

chapters.title: What Odile Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She reveals a bootleg cassette of Lena rehearsing the song — imperfect, alive — and hesitates to give it up because it holds her own grief too. Beat: shared mourning complicating alliance.

chapters.title: Tuning Fork Against Gavel
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He attempts one formal appeal anyway; it fails humiliatingly. Merrick's people offer hush money. Beat: nadir — justice must be invented, not requested.

chapters.title: The House Offers Terms
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Listening to the radiators one last full night, Ivo hears the house 'argue' for staying; he decides to bid on it with everything he has. Beat: commitment replacing tenancy in spirit and fact.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Among Ruins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Ivo, Odile, and neighborhood holdouts plan to perform Lena's song publicly on the final bus run, inviting press. Beat: rising hope with real risk of futility.

chapters.title: Merrick Hears His Name in the Wrong Mouth
chapters.summary: Merrick's POV. A leak reaches him; he threatens litigation and arrives in town unannounced. Beat: antagonist converges on the climax location.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Reroute
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sleepless, he cleans the house, says private goodbyes to each room, and nearly cancels everything out of fear. Beat: dread and tenderness intertwined.

chapters.title: Last Bus to the Old Neighborhood
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the packed final bus, Ivo stands and sings Lena's song aloud, voice cracking, while Odile plays the cassette over a portable player. Passengers join. Beat: climax — goodbye said properly, out loud.

chapters.title: The Man in the Back Row
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Merrick rides the same bus incognito; hearing the song sung by strangers, something breaks open. He does not apologize — but he does not deny it either, and a journalist records everything. Beat: ambiguous, humanizing turn.

chapters.title: Ownership
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo signs the deed to the house — owner at last — and hangs Lena's lyric page framed above the radiator. Beat: belonging achieved through act, not accident.

chapters.title: What the Pipes Carry Now
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Weeks later, the song circulates online, credited to Lena Whitlock; Merrick quietly settles royalties to her estate. Ivo teaches a neighborhood kid to hear houses. Beat: justice arrived sideways but arrived.

chapters.title: Coda: The House Is Listening
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On a winter evening Ivo plays the tuned piano while the radiators tick like applause; he speaks to Lena aloud, unhurried, home. Beat: resolution — memory housed, grief voiced, silence ended.
